newsitem.title: UK: Poor training UK's "Achilles' heel' - Industry body.
newsitem.headline: Poor training UK's "Achilles' heel' - Industry body.

text.p: - The Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said on Monday that poor education and training must not be allowed "to become Britain's Achilles' heel."

In a speech to open the CBI's annual conference here, CBI president Sir Colin Marshall said that "as a result of previous failures to address these issues, there is already a long tail of under-educated people in the workforce and on the dole."
Marshall said too much employer-funded training is focused on remedying deficiencies in basic skills.

"We must not allow poor education and training to become Britain's Achilles Heel lest we nobble ourselves in the race for global market success," said Marshall, who is chairman of British Airways Plc.
But Marshall also called for "labour market legislation which supports flexibility snd responsiveness and doesn't stand in the way of job creation."
